$comment: Explicit, dated, EXPIRING risk acceptances for npm audit findings that cannot reach production.
This file is not a mute button. An entry here changes nothing about whether a finding is
reported - the weekly audit still prints it, still counts it, and still notifies. What an
entry does is stop a finding that has NO available remediation from holding the gate red
forever, because a gate that can never go green carries no information and stops being read.
That is not hypothetical: `Trigger infra config guard` sat red for ten days in August 2026
and nobody noticed, which is how the fifth ClickHouse incident got its window.
- Only findings with ZERO production exposure may be acknowledged. A finding that reaches
shipped dependencies (`npm audit --omit=dev`) can never be acknowledged here; that gate
- Every entry needs reviewBy. Past that date the finding fails the gate again, whether or
not anything changed. Acceptance expires; it is not permanent.
- A NEW advisory that is not listed here fails the gate immediately, even if dev-only.
The point is that someone has to look at each one once.
- `evidence` must record how zero production exposure was established, not asserted.

reason: Stack-exhaustion DoS (CWE-674) from deeply nested brace patterns. Reachable only through the devDependency
trigger.dev@4.5.10 (the CLI), directly and via chokidar@3.6.0, i.e. file watching during `trigger dev`/deploy
over this repo's own source paths - never untrusted input, never the deployed worker.
No upstream remediation exists: braces@3.0.3 is the latest release and the advisory covers every version
(`<=3.0.3`), so no override can fix it. Re-evaluate when braces publishes a fix or trigger.dev drops chokidar@3.
evidence: npm ls braces --omit=dev: empty - not in the production dependency graph.
listed via docker create + export: 206 node_modules packages, braces/chokidar/trigger.dev = 0. Measured, not inferred.
